subject: Coding transect segments with no data for DSM

messages.author: 64e61d66e6c65728
messages.subject: Coding transect segments with no data for DSM
parts:
I am running a DSM for gorillas and the results being generated are not what I was expecting - different to what I estimate from predicted numbers form Distance 7.3. One issue may be the coding o the observation data for transect segments where there are no observations. For Distance 7.3 you give the transect label and effort and leave all observations blank. For the R Distance do I need to put in NAs or zeros or do I also leave the fields blank? If NAs are required how are these interpreted when covariables areused to model the density as presumably you want segments with no observations, and their associated covariables, to fit the model well.  I have tried to find the answer in documents that have been published and on this site but cannot - yet it must be something that people face regularly.

Andy

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Coding transect segments with no data for DSM
parts:
Andy

I can't guarantee the differences you are seeing between dsm in R and DSM in Distance 7.3 are the result of data formatting issues, but that seems a good place to start.

For an example of data organisation for the R package dsm, have a look at the Gulf of Mexico spotted dolphin vignette on our website: http://distancesampling.org/R/vignettes/mexico-analysis.html

The beginning of the vignette shows the data needed for a dsm analysis.  You will see there are actually three elements to the data:

- `segdata` containing information (including covariates) for **all** segments (with or without detections)
- `distdata` with information about the detections (group size, perpendicular distance, etc)
- `obsdata` describing segments in which detections were made.

No need for NAs.  There is also a `preddata` data object describing covariates in each cell of the study area, for use in prediction
